raw_case_text:
A 73-year-old female patient was admitted on January 22, 2024, with a 2-year history of recurrent thoracolumbar pain and fever. Two years prior, she was diagnosed with a thoracic vertebral infection at a local hospital and achieved symptom resolution after treatment with ceftoperazone/sulbactam. Six months before admission (August 2023), symptoms recurred. Chest CT revealed bilateral pulmonary inflammatory lesions, right pleural effusion, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, vascular calcifications (aorta/coronary arteries), and minor pericardial effusion (Figures 1A1,A2). Thoracic MRI demonstrated pathological fractures at T7-T8 vertebrae, bone marrow edema at T6, and degenerative thoracolumbar changes (Figure 2A). Symptoms improved following vancomycin therapy.
Three months prior (October 2023), the patient experienced post-COVID-19 exacerbation with dyspnea. Despite a 15-day course of intermittent steroids (dexamethasone 0.325 mg, oral, twice a day or methylprednisolone 4 mg, oral, twice a day) and antibiotics, symptoms persisted, culminating in acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis.
Five days before admission (January 18, 2024), bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) mNGS by Hangzhou Genetron Medical Laboratory detected: Pneumocystis jirovecii: 29,036 sequences (21.95% abundance), Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex: 2,544 sequences (1.92% abundance).
The patient was initiated on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (SMZ-Co 0.48 g, oral, twice a day) and transferred to a tuberculosis specialty hospital for suspected coinfection management.
The patient has a history of hypertension treated with bisoprolol and amlodipine (5 mg, oral, once a day) and diabetes mellitus managed with insulin aspart and glargine. Pre-admission evaluations (December 30, 2023) showed: negative serum HIV antibody, serum (1, 3)-beta-D-glucan <37.5 pg./mL (negative: <70 pg./mL), Aspergillus galactomannan antigen 0.11 (negative: <0.5), and lymphocytopenia (0.38 x 109/L, January 13, 2024). A thoracic MRI (December 28, 2023, Hangzhou Hospital of TCM) revealed T7-T8 vertebral destruction with abscess (Figure 2B). On January 24, 2024, a C-arm-guided biopsy of the vertebral lesion (Figure 3A) yielded pus and hemorrhagic fluid; subsequent testing confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC)-positive, rifampicin-sensitive, and positive MTB DNA/RNA. A lung lesion biopsy (January 30, 2024; Figures 3A,B) and tissue NGS (Hangzhou ADICON Lab) detected overwhelming Mycobacterium dominance (73,211 sequences, 87.07% abundance; MTBC: 72,040, 85.68%). During hospitalization, bilateral lower limb weakness developed (right: Grade 1; left: Grade 3). On February 15, 2024, under general anesthesia, T6-T8 interbody fusion, lesion resection, and pedicle screw fixation were performed, revealing severe osteolysis, necrotic bone, and extensive granulomatous tissue in spinal canals. Necrotic debris and granulomas were excised for histopathology (Figure 4).
Following surgery, the patient was transferred to the ICU for monitoring. Postoperatively, she exhibited Grade 1 bilateral lower limb muscle strength, clear consciousness, and impaired cough reflex. Treatment included intensified anti-infective therapy, nutritional support, and physical rehabilitation. On March 3, 2024, the endotracheal tube was removed, and high-flow nasal oxygen with humidification was initiated, though expectoration remained poor. Upon family request, the patient was transferred to another facility on March 7, 2024, where a regimen of rifampicin (0.45 g/day) orally, isoniazid 0.3 g/day, linezolid, oral, twice a day, and post-dialysis amikacin (standard dosing) was continued. Subsequent pulmonary improvement was observed (Figure 3). During hospitalization, anti infection and anti tuberculosis measures were administered (Figure 5), as well as changes in relevant indicators before and after treatment (Figure 6).
BALF Metagenomic NGS Results (April 2, 2024 | Hangzhou Jieyi Medical Laboratory).
Dominant Pathogens:
Klebsiella pneumoniae: 64,274 sequences (31.40% abundance),
Klebsiella spp.: 85,291 sequences (41.65% abundance),
Elizabethkingia anophelis: 13,244 sequences (6.47% abundance).
Additional Findings:
Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex: 279 sequences (0.15% abundance),
Staphylococcus aureus: 487 sequences (0.24% abundance),
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: 49 sequences (0.03% abundance),
Human herpesvirus 5 (CMV): 2,799 sequences (1.38% abundance).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 73-year-old female on maintenance hemodialysis was admitted on January 22, 2024, with a 2-year history of recurrent thoracolumbar pain and fever and a 3-month history of post-COVID-19 dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two years prior to admission, the patient was treated at a local hospital with cefoperazone/sulbactam for a thoracic vertebral infection with temporary symptom relief. Six months prior to admission (August 2023), her thoracolumbar pain and fever recurred, with thoracic MRI showing T7–T8 pathological fractures and T6 marrow edema, which transiently improved with vancomycin. Three months prior to admission (October 2023), she developed persistent post-COVID-19 dyspnea and acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis after receiving a 15-day course of intermittent oral steroids (dexamethasone 0.325 mg BID or methylprednisolone 4 mg BID) and antibiotics. Five days before referral (January 18, 2024), bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) mNGS at an outside hospital detected both Pneumocystis jirovecii (29,036 reads) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (2,544 reads), prompting initiation of oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (SMZ-Co 0.48 g BID) and transfer to a tuberculosis specialty hospital.
subjective.past_medical_history: Thoracic vertebral osteomyelitis/spondylodiscitis (2-year history with T7–T8 pathological fractures); post-COVID-19 acute-on-chronic renal failure requiring maintenance hemodialysis (since October 2023); hypertension; diabetes mellitus.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic recurrent thoracolumbar back pain, fever, and dyspnea (subsequently developed acute bilateral lower extremity weakness during hospitalization). Home medications included bisoprolol, amlodipine (5 mg PO qd), insulin aspart, insulin glargine, and recently started SMZ-Co (0.48 g PO bid).

objective.physical_examination: During hospitalization, the patient developed progressive paraparesis with right lower limb muscle strength Grade 1 and left lower limb muscle strength Grade 3 (postoperatively Grade 1 bilaterally with clear consciousness and impaired cough reflex).
objective.routine_investigations: Pre-admission laboratory tests (December 30, 2023 – January 13, 2024): Negative serum HIV antibody; lymphocytopenia with absolute lymphocyte count 0.38 x 10^9/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Pre-admission fungal biomarkers (December 30, 2023): Serum (1,3)-beta-D-glucan <37.5 pg/mL (negative <70 pg/mL) and Aspergillus galactomannan 0.11 (negative <0.5). Pre-admission chest CT (August 2023) and thoracic spine MRIs (August & December 28, 2023): Bilateral pulmonary inflammatory lesions, right pleural effusion, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, minor pericardial effusion, and T7–T8 vertebral destruction with paravertebral/epidural abscess and T6 bone marrow edema. Pre-admission BALF mNGS (January 18, 2024): Detected Pneumocystis jirovecii (29,036 sequence reads, 21.95% relative abundance) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (2,544 sequence reads, 1.92% abundance). Inpatient C-arm-guided T7–T8 vertebral biopsy (January 24, 2024) and lung lesion biopsy with tissue mNGS (January 30, 2024): Vertebral pus/fluid confirmed rifampicin-sensitive MTBC with positive MTB DNA/RNA; lung biopsy tissue NGS detected overwhelming Mycobacterium dominance (73,211 reads, 87.07% abundance; MTBC 72,040 reads, 85.68% abundance); spinal surgical histopathology (February 15, 2024) confirmed caseating/necrotizing granulomatous osteomyelitis. Follow-up BALF mNGS (April 2, 2024): Complete clearance of P. jirovecii, with residual MTBC (279 reads, 0.15%) and secondary airway flora/pathogens including Klebsiella spp. (85,291 reads; K. pneumoniae 64,274 reads), Elizabethkingia anophelis (13,244 reads), CMV (2,799 reads), S. aureus (487 reads), and P. aeruginosa (49 reads).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated pulmonary and T6–T8 spinal tuberculosis (Pott's disease with pathological fracture, epidural abscess, and paraparesis; confirmed by vertebral and lung biopsy pathology, MTB DNA/RNA, and tissue mNGS showing 72,040 MTBC reads) co-infected with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed by 29,036 P. jirovecii reads on baseline BALF mNGS) following corticosteroid therapy and hemodialysis. Plan and clinical course: Treated with oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (SMZ-Co 0.48 g BID) for PJP alongside four-drug anti-tuberculosis therapy consisting of oral rifampicin (0.45 g/day), isoniazid (0.3 g/day), oral linezolid (twice daily), and post-dialysis amikacin. Due to progressive lower limb paralysis, she underwent T6–T8 surgical debridement, decompression, interbody fusion, and pedicle screw fixation on February 15, 2024, followed by ICU monitoring, extubation to HFNC on March 3, and transfer to a rehabilitation facility on March 7, 2024, with subsequent radiographic pulmonary improvement and clearance of P. jirovecii on repeat BALF mNGS (April 2, 2024).
